hints.title: Subsequent Node Reference Preservation
hints.text: Reversing a link breaks the reference to the subsequent node. What must be retained before modifying the reference of the current node?

hints.title: Three Temporary Node References
hints.text: Store the next node in a temporary reference before redirecting the current node's next pointer to the previous node.

hints.title: Iterative Link Reversal Procedure
hints.text: Initialize prev = None and curr = head. While curr is not null, save next_node = curr.next, point curr.next to prev, advance prev = curr, and advance curr = next_node. Return prev as the new head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def reverseList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        prev = None
        curr = head
        while curr:
            next_node = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = next_node
        return prev
```

variables: N: number of nodes in the linked list (0 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Single pass visiting each node exactly once, updating pointers in-place.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting all values in an array and creating new nodes takes O(N) extra space and allocates new nodes rather than reversing links in-place.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative 3-pointer reversal achieves O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space without recursion stack overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: In-place pointer reversal with O(1) extra space, handling empty list (head == None) and single-node list, clean loop termination.

solutions.approach: Iterative Pointer Rewiring in O(1) Space
